result.rationale: The diff verifiably changes /groups/:name/members: previously `members = group.users.order(...)` with no limit for non-automatic groups (and 200 for automatic); now `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is always applied. Consumers of this public endpoint (e.g. anything using groups/:name/members.json) would now silently receive only 50 members by default. Whether this is intentional pagination or a breaking change is a review-relevant concern; the diff updates the Discourse frontend to paginate, but no versioning or compatibility note is provided for external consumers.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `GroupsController#members` now applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` for all groups and always does `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned the full unpaginated list and automatic groups defaulted to 200 (`limit = (params[:limit] || 200)`). This is an intentional pagination/API behavior change (also reflected by new `meta` in the JSON response and UI paging), but it is a potentially breaking change for any consumers assuming the endpoint returns all members by default.
